question: Which of the following tribal communities was primarily involved in the Chuar Rebellion in the Jungle Mahals region?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhumji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Chuar Rebellion (1767–1809) was a tribal uprising in the Jungle Mahals region of present-day West Bengal and Jharkhand.
 
• The rebellion was primarily led by the **Bhumji tribal community**, along with other tribal groups like the Santhals and Kurmis.
 
• The British East India Company’s exploitative revenue policies and increased taxes on forest produce triggered the rebellion.
 
• The Bhumji chiefs, particularly the leaders of the **Midnapore and Manbhum regions**, played a significant role in organizing the resistance.
 
• The rebellion was also marked by the participation of local zamindars and peasants who were discontented with colonial economic policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chuar Rebellion Context:**

 
 
• The term 'Chuar' was used by the British to describe the tribal insurgents and forest dwellers of the region.
 
• The rebellion was fueled by colonial interference in traditional tribal ways of life and exploitation of natural resources.
 
 
 
• **Key Leaders:**
 
 
• Prominent leaders of the rebellion included Raghunath Mahato and Durjan Singh.
 
• They mobilized tribal warriors and peasants against British forces.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• The rebellion was suppressed by the British, but it highlighted the widespread resistance to colonial policies in tribal regions.
 
• It paved the way for subsequent tribal uprisings like the Santhal Rebellion (1855–56).
 
 
 
• **Jungle Mahals:**
 
 
• The Jungle Mahals region included parts of present-day Purulia, Bankura, and Midnapore districts in West Bengal.
 
• The area was rich in forests and inhabited by several tribal communities.
